area: Updates, meetings, activity, tickets, chat & notifications

rows.feature: Post a progress update from the project
rows.what: A studio member presses + Post Update on the Overview's Progress Updates card to post a site update for the client.
rows.v1: Project › Overview › Progress Updates › + Post Update
rows.v2: Project › Client › Updates › Post an update; Overview › With {client} › Post an update; the header's filled button when posting is the next step

rows.feature: What an update holds: title, words, photos, videos, documents
rows.what: Title (120), plain details (1,000), photos stored as text inside the update, and a video or documents saved by their name only (never uploaded).
rows.v2: Project › Client › Updates › Post an update (the composer)
rows.how: Up to 12 photos, videos, PDFs and Office files, each uploaded for real into Files › Site updates (6 MB a video or document); the words take formatting; closing with something typed asks “Discard this update?” (1.0 threw it away silently).

rows.feature: Preview the update as the client will see it
rows.what: A Preview step shows the client's card (chips, title, words, photos) before posting; shown only when the studio's portal is on.
rows.v2: Composer › Preview (“As {client} sees it”); a card's See it as the client

rows.feature: Post from a phone on site
rows.what: Below 1024px a floating camera button opens a simpler composer: a message plus photos or videos from the rear camera; the title is invented as “Update for {client}”.
rows.v1: Project (phone, tablet) › floating camera button › Post Update
rows.v2: Project (phone) › site bar › Photos (while In progress); the composer opens photos-first
rows.how: One composer at every width; on a phone it starts with the camera and the photos and takes the running milestone's name. Pictures upload for real (1.0 kept browser-only addresses that broke when the tab closed) and the review rule applies (1.0's phone post ignored it and the handover lock).

rows.feature: Post an update from a milestone
rows.what: A milestone's action menu on the Gantt has Post Update, opening the dialog with that milestone already picked.
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › the band after a milestone starts or is marked done › Post an update; or pick the milestone in the composer
rows.how: The milestone's own panel has no Post update; the Schedule offers it when a milestone starts or is done (opening the composer with it picked), and any update can be tied to any milestone in the composer.

rows.feature: Post an update when a milestone is completed
rows.what: The milestone completion dialog's third step and the invoice drawer's optional box save an update “Milestone completed: {milestone}” with the typed words (never linked to the milestone).
rows.v1: Finance › milestone completion dialog › Post Update; invoice drawer › Post update
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › Mark {milestone} done sheet › add photos
rows.how: The Mark done sheet's photos post as “{milestone} is done”, linked to the milestone, under the update review rule; a Done waiting for approval carries them and posts them as whoever asked.

rows.feature: “This completes a payment milestone” tick on an update
rows.what: Ticked, a post rang the client's bell that the milestone was complete and drafted an invoice for its share, without marking the milestone done (and did nothing from the Gantt).
rows.v1: Post Update dialog › This completes a payment milestone
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › Mark done → the stage's invoice turns Ready to send (bell “An invoice is ready to send”)
rows.how: An update no longer drives money: marking the milestone Done makes its payment stage ready to bill and tells the team.

rows.feature: Tie an update to a milestone
rows.what: An optional Linked milestone on the update, meant to show as a chip (in 1.0 the chip never appeared).
rows.v2: Composer › Milestone; the card and the client's card show it

rows.feature: Updates need review before the client sees them
rows.what: On by default: a non-owner's post waits “Pending review”, an owner's goes out at once; a studio can switch review off.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflow Rules › Progress review required
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Updates need review before the client sees them
rows.how: An Admin's post also goes out at once.

rows.feature: Name extra reviewers
rows.what: Members listed as progress-update approvers (and members' own workflow overrides) approve updates and post without review.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Updates need review… › Who reviews › Add a reviewer
rows.how: Owners and Admins always review; named Designers or Managers review too and their posts go out at once. 1.0's per-member overrides become this one list.

rows.feature: A held update reaches its reviewer
rows.what: A held post creates a “Review progress update” task for the first approver (or the earliest owner) in /tasks; with no approver it publishes anyway.
rows.v1: /tasks › Progress Review task; Overview › Progress Updates › Pending review row
rows.v2: In review on the update; Overview › Needs you › Needs your OK; Projects › To do › Needs my review; the bell's row (Approve · Send back); the Client tab's count
rows.how: No task: every Owner, Admin and named reviewer is told and can answer from the bell, the Overview, the listing or the card.

rows.feature: Approve a held update
rows.what: One press publishes it to the client and stamps the publish time (through the review task when one exists).
rows.v1: Overview › Progress Updates › Approve; /tasks › Progress Review
rows.v2: Client › Updates › card › Approve; Overview › Needs you › Approve; the bell › Approve

rows.feature: Send a held update back with a reason
rows.what: Reject with a reason: the update stays hidden with no chip, its poster is not told, cannot edit or resubmit, and who reviewed is never recorded.
rows.v2: Card › Send back (reason required) → Sent back; the author's Edit · Resubmit
rows.how: A sent-back update shows its reason, rings its author's bell and goes again with Resubmit; who reviewed and when are kept.

rows.feature: Who may post, review and remove, checked on the server
rows.what: The screen limits review and delete to owners, but the server took post, review, unpublish and delete from any studio member, with no stage, lock or archive check.
rows.v2: Every update action (refusals say the rule)
rows.how: The server checks every action: the project's team, their Managers, Owners and Admins post, edit, withdraw and delete; Owners, Admins and named reviewers review; whoever cannot open the lead is refused.

rows.feature: Take a published update off the client's view
rows.what: Unpublish (an unlabelled icon, no confirm) works only until any linked client opens the portal after it was published; the update becomes a draft that can never be published again.
rows.v2: Card ⋮ › Withdraw (Undo); a Withdrawn card › Publish again
rows.how: Allowed until the client has had that update on screen (not the whole portal); Undo right after; a withdrawn update can be published again.

rows.feature: Delete an update
rows.what: An owner deletes any update for good after a confirm strip; a held one leaves its review task open.
rows.v2: Card ⋮ › Delete (Undo)
rows.how: Only an update the client cannot see (a published one is withdrawn first); the team, Owners and Admins; Undo brings it back; its review notices go with it.

rows.feature: Every update in one list, with search
rows.what: “View all {n} updates” opens a side sheet whose search covers title, details, author and milestone.
rows.v2: Project › Client › Updates (state chips, search, grouped by day)

rows.feature: Photo viewer and before/after compare
rows.what: Photos open full screen; with two or more, Compare puts the first two in a before/after slider.
rows.v2: Update card › Compare before and after (either photo can be changed); photos open in the viewer

rows.feature: Progress Updates card on the Overview
rows.what: The three newest updates with their chips and review actions, a + Post Update button and View all.
rows.v2: Overview › With {client} (“Last told {client} n days ago” · Post an update); updates to review in Needs you
rows.how: The card was folded into With {client} and Needs you; the full list is Client › Updates.

rows.feature: Posting after handover
rows.what: With the studio's handover lock on, a Closed project's Post Update is disabled and review buttons hidden (the phone button ignores the lock).
rows.v2: Client › Updates stays open on a completed project
rows.how: Completing a project locks its schedule and money only; updates can still be posted, under the review rule.

rows.feature: The studio hears about a post
rows.what: Every post rings owners, admins and designers (a held one only its approver) by bell and email; the email always says “Pending review” with a Review button.
rows.v2: Bell “A project update needs review” (reviewers) · “An update goes out to the client” (the project's members)
rows.how: Two notices instead of one: reviewers hear only of updates waiting for them; the project's members hear when one goes out; emails follow Settings › Notifications.

rows.feature: The client's bell rings for a new update
rows.what: When an update is published (at once or on approval) each linked client gets a “New project update” bell row with its title.
rows.v2: Client portal › bell › “New update: {title}” (read once they open it)

rows.feature: Updates on the old no-login pay link
rows.what: The public /pay/{token} page also returned the newest 20 approved updates.
rows.v2: Client portal › Updates; the no-login invoice link shows the invoice only
rows.how: Updates are read on the portal alone.

rows.feature: Automatic “Schedule updated” updates
rows.what: Publishing moved milestones posted one update each to the client — “Previously {dates} → Now {dates}”.
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › Share N changes
rows.how: No automatic posts: the share sends the client the list of what changed (their bell and an email) and keeps the snapshot they see.

rows.feature: Automatic update when more time is asked on a milestone
rows.what: With “Auto-update on extension” on, an extension request posts “Timeline extension requested: {milestone}” to the client.
rows.v2: Schedule › milestone › More time asked → Approve offers “Draft an update for {client} with the new day” (ticked)
rows.how: Nothing reaches the client when time is asked; approving it can write a draft update “New finish date for {milestone}” that the studio sends.

rows.feature: Recent updates across projects on the Dashboard
rows.what: Owners see the latest progress updates of every project, each opening its project.
rows.how: The Dashboard is not built yet.

rows.feature: “Site Update” chip on the chat home
rows.what: Picks a project and drafts a site-visit update with the assistant.
rows.how: The Dashboard is not built yet.

rows.feature: Meeting Summary card on the project
rows.what: The newest AI meeting brief for the project: date, a “Deal” score, three summary lines, three top actions and “+ n earlier meetings”.
rows.how: Held for the Meetings mocks; the lead's Meetings tab and Meeting quick link are hidden.

rows.feature: Launch the meeting co-pilot from a project
rows.what: Log Meeting › Launch Co-pilot: a consent check, then the live co-pilot for the project's lead (objective, live transcription and insights); its brief lands on the project.
rows.v1: Project › Overview › Meeting Summary › Log Meeting › Launch Co-pilot
rows.how: Tools › Meeting Copilot is a coming-soon tile; its credit price (Co-Pilot, 10 min) waits in the plans.

rows.feature: Upload a meeting recording for a brief
rows.what: Pick an audio file (up to 25 MB), confirm consent; it is transcribed and summarised into a brief on the project within minutes (no credits charged).
rows.v1: Meeting Summary › Log Meeting › Upload recording

rows.feature: Open the full brief and every meeting
rows.what: “Open full brief” and “view all” open the co-pilot's analytics in a new tab (studio-wide, not this project's).
rows.v1: Meeting Summary › Open full brief / view all

rows.feature: Who sees meeting briefs
rows.what: Owners and admins see every meeting; anyone else sees only briefs from sessions they ran.

rows.feature: File a brief to a lead or project, save its facts to the lead
rows.what: A brief can be attached to a lead or a project, and chosen facts from it saved back onto the lead.
rows.v1: Co-pilot brief › Attach to / Save to lead

rows.feature: Weekly meeting analytics job
rows.what: Every Sunday a scheduled job rolls the week's ended co-pilot sessions into studio and member metrics.

rows.feature: Activity tab on the project
rows.what: A feed rebuilt on every read from twelve record types, one line per record whose words change as the record changes, capped per source, with lines that open nothing.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Activity
rows.how: A real log: each step is its own line at its own time, naming who did it and linking to the record, with a search; milestones, invites, edits and messages leave lines too.

rows.feature: Activity card on the Overview
rows.what: The five newest lines with “View all →” to the tab.
rows.v2: Overview › Recent activity (three lines, ↗ to Activity; folded behind Show on a phone)

rows.feature: Filter Activity by kind
rows.what: Chips All · Updates · Finance · Issues · Timeline (tasks, procurement and files had no chip).
rows.v2: Activity › chips: All · Schedule · Updates · Money · Choices · Tasks · Files · Notes · Floor plan · 3D layouts · Tickets · Messages · Compliance · Stage

rows.feature: “Show all n events”
rows.what: The tab shows 20 lines, then Show all reveals the rest of what was loaded (older records silently dropped by caps).
rows.v2: Activity lists every line, newest first
rows.how: No paging and no caps; the search box narrows it.

rows.feature: Lines for progress updates
rows.what: “{author} approved / rejected / posted progress update” — the author is credited with the reviewer's act.
rows.v2: Activity › Updates
rows.how: Drafted, posted, sent for review, approved, sent back, edited, withdrawn and deleted — each by whoever did it.

rows.feature: Lines for tasks
rows.what: “{assignee} created / completed / approved task”, dated at creation, naming the assignee whoever acted.
rows.v2: Activity › Tasks
rows.how: Each change to a task is its own line naming who made it, at the time it was made.

rows.feature: Lines for invoices and client payments
rows.what: System lines “Invoice {no} created / sent to client / fully paid” and “Payment received for {no}”, amounts without currency, shown to every member.
rows.v2: Activity › Money
rows.how: Each step of an invoice and payment is its own line with who did it and S$ amounts; members who may not see the project's money get none of them.

rows.feature: Lines for purchase orders, variation orders and expenses
rows.what: System lines for a PO's or VO's status and for expenses logged and reviewed.
rows.v2: Activity › Money

rows.feature: Lines for commission
rows.what: “Commission override set” and “{member} requested commission change” with the owner's answer, shown to every member.
rows.v2: Activity › Money
rows.how: Owners and Admins read every commission line; a member reads only the lines about their own commission.

rows.feature: Lines for tickets
rows.what: “Escalation “{subject}” opened ({priority})” or “… resolved”.
rows.v2: Activity › Tickets (raised, given to, escalated, resolved, reopened, closed)

rows.feature: Lines for files and the project's start
rows.what: “{uploader} uploaded {file} to {folder}” and “Project created” (System).
rows.v2: Activity › Files; the project's created line names who made it

rows.feature: The studio's list of every ticket
rows.what: Escalations page: Open / In progress / Resolved counts and an always-empty “Avg. resolution time”, a sortable table (ticket, subject, project, priority, status, assigned to, “Raised by” always —).
rows.v2: Projects › ⋮ › Tickets (with the count waiting on the studio)
rows.how: Cards naming the project and client, Open · Resolved and closed · All with counts, and a search; no sortable table and no average resolution time.

rows.feature: Filter tickets by priority, status and member
rows.what: A Filter popover with Priority, Status and Assigned To, and Clear All Filters.
rows.v2: Projects › Tickets › Open · Resolved and closed · All, search
rows.how: No filter by who looks after a ticket or by priority (the search covers number, subject, project, client and the person's name).

rows.feature: Who sees and handles tickets
rows.what: Every studio member sees every ticket of the studio and may change any.
rows.v2: Tickets on projects the member may open
rows.how: A ticket shows only to whoever may open its project (Who sees leads); the project's team, their Managers, Owners and Admins reply, assign, resolve and reopen.

rows.feature: The studio logs a new ticket
rows.what: Subject, project, category, priority (Low…Critical), assignee and description; a note promises an SMS for Critical (none is sent); owners, admins and the assignee are told.
rows.v2: Project › Client › Tickets › New ticket
rows.how: Raised on a project in the client's own form (category, subject, what happened, up to 5 photos) plus Looked after by; it shows on the client's Issues at once; only the member it is given to is told.

rows.feature: Read a ticket's thread
rows.what: The ticket page: status, client and date; the “Original report” with its photos, then every reply marked Homeowner or Studio; a “From homeowner” badge.
rows.v2: Tickets › a ticket's drawer (the report, its facts, the thread with state lines)

rows.feature: Reply on a ticket, or leave an internal note
rows.what: A reply box (“Type a reply or internal note…”, Enter sends, emoji) where every reply reaches the client on a client's ticket; the attach buttons do nothing.
rows.v2: Ticket drawer › To the client · Internal note
rows.how: A reply can be an Internal note the client never sees; up to 5 photos travel with a reply.

rows.feature: Move a ticket: start, resolve, reopen
rows.what: Start Working (In progress), Mark Resolved and Re-open; the resolved time is stamped and cleared on reopen.
rows.v2: Ticket drawer › Mark resolved (a closing line the client reads, Undo) · Reopen
rows.how: In progress comes by itself with the studio's first reply or an assignment; resolving asks for a closing line; Closed is the client's own word.

rows.feature: Give a ticket to someone
rows.what: Assigned To is shown and a Re-assign button sits under it, which does nothing.
rows.v2: Ticket drawer › Looked after by
rows.how: Works, with Undo; the member it is given to hears it on the bell.

rows.feature: Ticket priority
rows.what: Four levels Low · Medium · High · Critical (a client's ticket is always Medium).
rows.v1: Escalations › New Ticket › Priority; list badge
rows.v2: Normal / Urgent; Ticket drawer › Escalate (a note)
rows.how: Two levels; Escalate marks it Urgent with a note, tells Owners and Admins and keeps the project in Needs attention until it is resolved.

rows.feature: AI Analysis on a ticket
rows.what: A panel with one fixed sentence about delay risk, not worked out from anything.

rows.feature: Proactive Alerts tab
rows.what: “ID Buddy continuously monitors all active projects…” over a list that is always empty.

rows.feature: Ticket categories
rows.what: The studio edits the category list (the server kept only four of the eight words the client could pick).
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › Ticket categories
rows.how: Eight default words, each kept as typed; a rename carries the tickets; a used one is retired, an unused one removed with Undo.

rows.feature: Ticket numbers with the studio's prefix
rows.what: T-{year}-{six digits from the clock}, its prefix set in Accounts › Document Numbering.
rows.v2: T-{YYYY}-{nnn}, counted per year across the studio
rows.how: The number counts up per year; there is no prefix setting (Settings › Finance › Document numbers has no ticket row).

rows.feature: A project's tickets and what they raise
rows.what: A ticket may carry a project; open ones count in the project's action items and health score.
rows.v2: Project › Client › Tickets (with its count); Needs attention “ticket escalated” / “waiting 2+ days”
rows.how: Every ticket belongs to a project and has its own view; an escalated ticket or one left waiting on the studio raises the project (also on hold); no health score.

rows.feature: The client reports an issue; the studio is told
rows.what: From the portal's Support tab a client files a ticket (category, subject, words, up to 5 photos) and the studio's roles hear “Escalation Created” at once.
rows.v2: Client portal › Issues › Report an issue → bell “A client reports an issue” (the project's members, else Owners and Admins)

rows.feature: The client replies or closes; the studio is told
rows.what: A client's reply and their Close (a browser confirm) notify the studio (escalation.replied, escalation.closed_by_homeowner).
rows.v2: Bell “A client answers on a ticket” (whoever looks after it, else the team)

rows.feature: The client hears the studio's reply or resolve
rows.what: Bell rows “New reply on {ticket}” and “Ticket resolved”; the resolve's client email is wired but no address is passed, so none goes.
rows.v2: Client portal › bell; Settings › Notifications › Messages to clients › The studio answers an issue (Email on)
rows.how: An email (or WhatsApp) now goes too, never for an internal note; it is recorded in Sent messages until a real provider is plugged in.

rows.feature: The studio's inbox of conversations
rows.what: /inbox lists every conversation in the studio, newest first, with a search and All · Unread · Escalations filters.
rows.v2: Rail › Messages (/chat)
rows.how: Every project conversation the member may see, unread first then newest, with unread counts, a rail badge and a search; no filter chips.

rows.feature: Chats with a lead, a contact or a group
rows.what: New Chat with a contact or a phone number (also from the lead drawer), New Group with several contacts, and studio-only chats.
rows.v2: Project › Client › Messages
rows.how: Only one conversation per project, between the client's household and the team; no chat with a lead before Won, no group or team-only chats.

rows.feature: Read and write in a conversation
rows.what: Messages with day dividers; inbound ones marked read when the chat is opened; the latest 50 per chat load (the portal side read the oldest 200).
rows.v2: Project › Client › Messages; Rail › Messages (the latest 200, Show earlier messages, a New line where unread start)

rows.feature: Send a file in a conversation
rows.what: Attach any file (kept in the chat's files) and it is sent as a message with its name and size.
rows.v2: Messages › composer: up to 3 photos (filed in Files › Messages)
rows.how: Photos only; no documents or videos in a message.

rows.feature: Voice notes, location, contact cards and emoji
rows.what: The composer records a voice note, shares a location or a phone contact, and has an emoji picker (each is sent as a text placeholder — no audio is kept).

rows.feature: Suggested replies
rows.what: A suggested reply under a client's last message, picked from fixed keyword-matched sentences.

rows.feature: Search inside a conversation
rows.what: Search in conversation with a count of matches.
rows.how: Messages are not searched, inside a conversation or from ⌘K — left for a later call.

rows.feature: Pin, mute and share a conversation
rows.what: Pin / Unpin, Mute (kept in that browser only), copy a link to the chat; an Archive button that does nothing.
rows.v1: Inbox › conversation header ⋮; details panel › Actions

rows.feature: A conversation's details: project, files, members
rows.what: A side panel with the project (View Project), the shared files and the members, who can be added or removed.
rows.v2: Rail › Messages › Open project; photos in the project's Files › Messages
rows.how: Who is in the conversation follows portal access and the project's team — nobody is added by hand; its files live in the project's Files.

rows.feature: Call the client from a conversation
rows.what: Call (a phone link) and Video call (no action) in the conversation's header.
rows.v2: Project › info column › the client's phone
rows.how: Video call had no action in 1.0 and has none in 2.0.

rows.feature: The client writes from the portal; the studio is told
rows.what: The portal's Project Chat (off by default, polled every 5 s) lands in the studio's inbox; nobody in the studio is told of a client's message.
rows.v1: Client portal › Project Chat → studio Inbox
rows.v2: Client portal › Messages → bell “A client sends a message” (once per 15 minutes per conversation); the rail's Messages count
rows.how: The project's members are told; the conversation has its own portal section switch.

rows.feature: “Show chat history” when inviting the client
rows.what: A switch on the invite: the client sees messages from before they joined, or only after.
rows.v1: Invite to Portal › Show chat history

rows.feature: The studio's bell
rows.what: A drawer of notifications with All / Unread and Mark all read.
rows.v2: Rail › bell: Updates · Due, Mark all as read; approvals answered in the row
rows.how: Due reminders are listed apart and never counted as unread; an approval (update, invoice, Done, more time, PO, expense) is answered in its own row.

rows.feature: Choose channels for each kind of notice
rows.what: Per category (Projects, Invoices, POs, Finance ops, Tasks & escalations…) switches for In-app, Email and WhatsApp; owners get in-app and email by default.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Events and channels
rows.how: Switches per event, not per category, with their own defaults; Owners and Admins change them.

rows.feature: Choose who hears each kind of notice
rows.what: A Recipients popover per category with role ticks (owner · admin · designer · accounting); the record's assignees are always added.
rows.how: 2.0 shows each event's fixed Who, read-only.

rows.feature: Daily digest email
rows.what: A Digest tick per category holds non-critical notices and sends them as one email at 8 AM studio time.

rows.feature: The studio's own wording for each message
rows.what: Per event and channel, a template editor with variables, a preview and Reset.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Messages (Insert a field, preview)

rows.feature: Emails to studio members
rows.what: Each notice is emailed to its recipients through the email provider, spaced to its rate limit.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Sent messages lists each one
rows.how: Messages are written to the outbox, not sent; developers plug a real email service in with setDeliveryAdapter.

rows.feature: WhatsApp alerts to studio members
rows.what: Through 360dialog, only for events with approved templates (task assigned, due reminder, revision asked, VO answered, invoice overdue, payment received).
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Events and channels › WhatsApp; Sent messages
rows.how: Any event can have WhatsApp on; messages are recorded, not sent — a WhatsApp Business provider with approved templates is the developers'.

rows.feature: Sending safeguards
rows.what: Duplicates within 120 s are dropped, demo studios never send, an operator can pause a studio's own notices, and a large fan-out raises an alarm.
rows.v2: The delivery layer
rows.how: Each message is keyed so it never goes twice, the person who acted is never told, and chat and floor-plan notices have quiet windows; no demo-studio silence, operator pause or fan-out alarm.

rows.feature: Retry failed emails
rows.what: Emails that failed are tried again, up to three times, by the hourly job.

rows.feature: Schedule published: the studio hears
rows.what: Publishing the Gantt rings owners and admins (“Timeline Published to Homeowner”).
rows.v2: Bell “A schedule change waits for your approval” · “Your schedule ask is answered”; Activity's share line
rows.how: Owners and Admins hear of a share only when it waits for their approval; a share sent directly leaves an Activity line and no bell.

rows.feature: The client confirms a finished stage
rows.what: Owners, admins, designers and assignees hear “{client} approved {milestone}”.
rows.v2: Bell “A client confirms a finished stage”

rows.feature: The client says a stage is not right
rows.what: “{client} requested a revision on {milestone}” with their notes — critical, with a WhatsApp template.
rows.v2: Bell “A client says something is not right with a stage” (In app, Email, WhatsApp on)

rows.feature: A choice is shared
rows.what: “A new selection is ready for your pick” goes to the studio's own roles (no client address is passed).
rows.v2: The client is told: Messages to clients › A choice to make (Email on) + their bell
rows.how: The client, not the studio, hears of a shared choice.

rows.feature: The client picks an option
rows.what: Owners, admins and designers hear “The homeowner picked an option” (critical).
rows.v2: Bell “A client makes a choice” (and “A client says no to a choice”)

rows.feature: A priced pick drafts a variation order
rows.what: Owners and admins hear “Variation Order Auto-Drafted from Selection” (critical).
rows.v2: The pick's bell row; the draft waits in Money and the Overview's Needs you
rows.how: No separate notice: the pick's own row tells the team, and the drafted order is a Needs you row until it is sent.

rows.feature: The client answers a variation order
rows.what: Owners, admins and designers hear that the client approved or rejected a VO (critical, WhatsApp templates).
rows.v2: Bell “A client approves a variation order” · “A client declines a variation order” (with the reason)

rows.feature: The client answers the questionnaire
rows.what: The assigned designer and owner hear “{client} answered your scope questionnaire” (in-app).
rows.v2: Bell “A client answers the questionnaire”

rows.feature: The client is asked to fill the questionnaire
rows.what: Asking puts a row on the client's portal bell (in-app only).
rows.v2: Ask the client sends a WhatsApp in one press; the portal's What needs you lists the questions
rows.how: No bell row and no automatic email for the ask.

rows.feature: Floor-plan notices, both ways
rows.what: Plan shared, studio marks, client marks (bell only, one alert per side per plan per 15 minutes), client uploads a plan, client approves a layout.
rows.v2: Bell “A client marks up the floor plan” (15-minute quiet window) · “A client confirms a layout”; client's bell “A floor plan from your designer” · “Your designer replied”

rows.feature: Ask the client for their floor plan
rows.what: The studio's request emails the client to send their plan (always sent).

rows.feature: A task is assigned
rows.what: The assignee and the assigner hear it (bell, email, WhatsApp template); bulk-made tasks stay quiet.
rows.v2: Bell “A task is assigned to you”

rows.feature: A task is due in 30 minutes
rows.what: A reminder queued at creation for 30 minutes before the task's day and time (09:00 if none), sent by the 5-minute job; archiving a project cancels them.
rows.v2: Bell › Due › “Due in n min”; a running project's task also “Due tomorrow / in n days” at the alerts' lead time
rows.how: Worked out when the bell is read, not queued; a completed project's tasks stop ringing.

rows.feature: A milestone is coming due or late
rows.what: Proactive Alerts made review tasks for milestones nearing their date (lead time 1–30 days), and only while the Gantt was open.
rows.v2: Bell › Due › “Ends in n days: {milestone}” · “Overdue: {milestone}”; Settings › Projects › Schedule › Alerts lead time
rows.how: Bell rows from the dates for the project's members, whatever page is open; no review tasks.

rows.feature: An invoice is sent: the studio hears
rows.what: Owners and admins get “Invoice Sent” (critical) whenever an invoice goes to the client.
rows.v2: Bell “Your invoice is approved and sent” (the submitter); Activity's invoice line
rows.how: Only the member whose invoice an approver sent is told; Owners and Admins get no notice when an invoice goes out.

rows.feature: An invoice waits for approval
rows.what: The approver hears “Invoice Awaiting Approval” (critical) when invoice approval is on.
rows.v2: Bell “An invoice needs approval” (and “Your invoice is sent back” / “approved and sent” to the submitter)

rows.feature: Remind the approver
rows.what: A nudge to the approver about a waiting invoice, bell only, at most once an hour per person and three a day per invoice.
rows.v2: Money › a submitted invoice's band or ⋮ › Remind the approvers (once an hour per person)

rows.feature: A client's payment comes in
rows.what: Owners and admins hear “Payment Received” (WhatsApp template) when the client submits proof or the studio records a payment.
rows.v2: Bell “A client says they have paid” (whoever confirms payments) · “A client’s payment is confirmed” (the project's members)
rows.how: Two notices: the confirmer hears of a client's proof; the project's members hear once it is confirmed.

rows.feature: An invoice is overdue: the studio hears
rows.what: The nightly job tells owners and admins “Invoice {n} for {client} is overdue — {total}” (WhatsApp template), linking to Finance › Operations.
rows.v2: Bell › Due › “An invoice is overdue” (the project's members); Money's red band; Needs attention
rows.how: Worked out from the due day whenever read, for the project's members (in-app by default).

rows.feature: A purchase order goes to the vendor
rows.what: The vendor is emailed the PO automatically and owners and admins hear “PO Sent to Vendor” (critical).
rows.v2: Money › purchase order › Send: WhatsApp with the PO's no-login link, opened on the press
rows.how: No automatic email to the vendor and no studio notice on a send; a submitter hears “Your purchase order is approved and sent”.

rows.feature: The vendor answers a purchase order
rows.what: Owners and admins hear “PO Acknowledged by Vendor” or “PO Rejected by Vendor”.
rows.v2: Bell “A vendor answers a purchase order” (accepted, changes asked or declined) to its maker and the project's members

rows.feature: An expense is submitted
rows.what: Owners and admins hear of every submitted expense.
rows.v2: Bell “An expense needs approval” (when Settings › Finance › Costs asks for it) · “Your expense is answered”
rows.how: Told only when the expense waits for approval; the answer goes back to whoever logged it.

rows.feature: Commission is paid
rows.what: Owners hear “Commission of {amount} paid for {project}”.
rows.v2: Bell “Your commission is paid” to the member paid
rows.how: The member paid is told, not the owner.

rows.feature: The accounting link needs attention
rows.what: Owners and admins are told (critical) when the accounting connection can no longer refresh, so sync has stopped.
rows.v2: Bell “Xero needs you” (a push failed and waits for Retry)
rows.how: Derived from the prototype's simulated Xero push; a real connection and its expiry are the developers'.

rows.feature: An invoice is sent: the client is told
rows.what: The invoice email always goes to the lead's address, and the portal's bell gets “Invoice {n} sent”.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Messages to clients › An invoice is sent (Email on); the portal's bell
rows.how: The bell row is real; the email (or WhatsApp) is recorded in Sent messages, not sent; it goes to everyone the portal is open to and waits while an Undo is offered.

rows.feature: Something to sign or approve: the client is told
rows.what: Signature requests and composed contracts are always emailed to the client; a variation order waiting rings their bell.
rows.v2: Messages to clients › Something to sign or approve; the portal's bell (agreement to sign, variation to approve, quote shared)
rows.how: The bell rows are real; the email is recorded in Sent messages until a real provider is plugged in.

rows.feature: The schedule is shared: the client is told
rows.what: The first linked client with an email gets “Your timeline has been updated” (a studio switch).
rows.v2: Messages to clients › The schedule is shared; the portal's bell “Your schedule is ready / has changed”
rows.how: Goes to everyone the portal is open to; the bell row is real, the email is recorded, not sent.

rows.feature: A payment is confirmed: the client is told
rows.what: Bell rows “Payment for {n} confirmed” and “Receipt {r} for {n}”.
rows.v2: The portal's bell (payment confirmed) + Messages to clients › A payment is confirmed (Email on)
rows.how: One bell row for both, and an email with the receipt on their page (recorded, not sent, until a real provider is plugged in).

rows.feature: A milestone's status changes: the client is told
rows.what: Every milestone status change rang the client's bell (“Milestone complete: {name}”), sent from the browser.
rows.v2: The portal's bell “Your schedule has changed” after a share; “Confirm …” when the studio asks
rows.how: Nothing about the schedule reaches the client until the studio shares changes or asks them to confirm a stage.

rows.feature: A floor plan is shared or asked for: the client is emailed
rows.what: Sharing a plan (a studio switch) and asking for the client's plan (always) email the client.
rows.v2: The portal's bell “A floor plan from your designer”
rows.how: Bell only; floor plans are not among the client email events.

rows.feature: Choose which messages reach clients
rows.what: Customer Notifications: a switch per informational client event; functional ones (invoice, signing, PO) always go, in fixed words.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Messages to clients
rows.how: Every client event has Email and WhatsApp switches and its own editable words with a preview; none is forced on.

rows.feature: Who gets the client's messages
rows.what: The lead's email address, or the first linked client with one.
rows.v2: Everyone the home's portal is open to
rows.how: The client and their invited household; nothing goes while the portal is paused, before the invite, or for a section the studio switched off.

rows.feature: Nightly invoice-overdue job
rows.what: At 06:00 SGT, marks sent and part-paid invoices past due as overdue across all studios and alerts each.
rows.v2: No job: overdue is worked out from the due day whenever read
rows.how: The invoice's state, the studio's bell, the client's bell (“due in 3 days”, “overdue”) and Needs attention all derive from the date.

rows.feature: Five-minute job that sends scheduled reminders
rows.what: Claims due reminders and sends them (up to 100 a run); skips demo studios and holds paused ones.
rows.v2: Reminders' emails and WhatsApps go when a member opens their bell; held client messages are released on the next delivery
rows.how: In production a sweep must run deliverDerived and releaseHeldMessages for every member — left for the developers (the comment in delivery.ts).

rows.feature: Five-minute accounting sync job
rows.what: Sends each studio's queued invoices, payments, bills and credit notes to Xero, QuickBooks or Zoho.
rows.v2: Company › Integrations › Xero (simulated push with Retry)
rows.how: The push is simulated; a real connection and its scheduled sync are the developers'.

rows.feature: Daily exchange-rate job
rows.what: Refreshes exchange rates daily so finance reports can convert other countries' amounts into the studio's currency.

notes: Reviewer 6 wrote that 1.0 emailed the client when a ticket was resolved; the status route passes no client address, so in practice only the client's bell row went (UC-062). The inbox's “Escalations” filter and banner, its Archive and Video call buttons, the unmounted Chat Highlights card (D-177), the offline post_update queue (J-237), the unused homeowner notification preferences (J-53) and the usage-analytics events (D-89, J-236) are 1.0 dead code or plumbing and have no rows. Closure (D-238…D-357), the portal's own Issues / Messages / Updates pages and the Leads-only notices and jobs (lead events, price drift, Gmail polling, usage roll-ups) are left to their readers; client-side rows here cover only what triggers a notice. Email and WhatsApp in 2.0 are recorded in Sent messages and never sent, so every “email” row depends on the developers' setDeliveryAdapter and a sweep job. Nothing was run in either app — every row was checked by reading the code.
